claims.claim: The deepest hole humans have ever dug
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z, full text at https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (published 3 Feb 2026)
claims.note: Lobanov: "In 1990, the maximum depth was reached — 12262 m, which has not been surpassed so far." Zhu & Huang (Feb 2026): SG-3 "remains the deepest vertical borehole ever attempted, reaching 12,262 m"; the deepest others they list are X-1 (11,156 m) and SDTK-1 (10,910 m). To try to break it, a web search (not a source) found nothing deeper completed by Nov 2026, only planned Chinese wells. 'Deepest' is right because it means vertical depth: extended-reach wells that are longer by measured depth are not deeper. 'Dug' for 'drilled' is framing.

claims.claim: Hook at second two: a viewer who swipes after "The deepest hole humans have ever dug" (word 'dug' ends ~2.1 s), having seen the 1987 USSR stamp labelled "THE KOLA BOREHOLE, USSR" / "DEEPEST HOLE" (cutout) or a derrick over ground in section (illustrated), leaves believing the Kola borehole is the deepest hole humans have made
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z, full text at https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (published 3 Feb 2026); public/cutout/hole/stamp.jpg viewed
claims.note: True as stated (see claim 1). The popular myth that the Kola hole was stopped by 'sounds from hell' is not touched. The other popular error, that longer extended-reach wells are 'deeper', is avoided by saying 'deepest'. The stamp reads "кольская сверхглубокая скважина ... ПОЧТА СССР 1987 10к", so the label is right.

claims.claim: ...was finished with a bit narrower than a dinner plate.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Clarke et al., USGS Open-File Report 86-517 (1986), https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext, 255 pp.); Met Museum collection API, https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/201074
claims.note: Lobanov: turbine "with a 214 mm drill bit" (RU: "с буровой коронкой диаметром 214 мм"). Fig. 5c (actual well design): "d 215,9 мм 12262 м", open hole ("открытый ствол") below "d 245 мм 8770 м". USGS: "ISM-214,3/60T ... designed for turbodrilling with coring". Met 51.86.100 'Dinner plate': "Diameter: 10 1/16 in. (25.6 cm)". 21.4-21.6 cm < 25.6 cm. 'Finished with' limits the claim to the last stretch; higher up the hole is wider (720/325/245 mm).

claims.claim: It took the Soviet Union about twenty years.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z, full text at https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (published 3 Feb 2026)
claims.note: Lobanov: "Drilling was started on May 24, 1970"; "In 1990, the maximum depth was reached — 12262 m"; also "As of 05/01/1991, the well depth was 12262 m". Zhu & Huang: "reaching 12,262 m between 1970 and 1989". That is 19-20 years, so 'about twenty' is right. The USSR still existed in 1989-90.

claims.claim: It goes down twelve kilometres.

claims.note: 12,262 m in both sources, rounded down to 'twelve kilometres'. The present tense is acceptable: Lobanov says the well was "mothballed" (RU "законсервирована"), not filled.

claims.claim: And it never made it through the crust.
claims.source_checked: Clarke et al., USGS Open-File Report 86-517 (1986), https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext, 255 pp.); Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. claims.note: USGS: "Crustal thickness in the vicinity of the corehole was shown to be about 40 km"; "The average depth of the Mohorovicic discontinuity on the Kola Peninsula is 37 km with a range of 28 to 40 km". Zhu & Huang: "Despite not penetrating the Moho". 12.262 km is well short of 28-40 km.

claims.claim: At the bottom, the rock was over two hundred degrees.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z, full text at https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (published 3 Feb 2026)
claims.note: Lobanov: "the real temperature in the borehole at a depth of 10 km reached 180°С, and at a depth of about 12 km, the temperature values reached 212°С, instead of the assumed 120°С". Zhu & Huang: "bottom-hole temperatures of 212 °C"; "212 °C at 12 km". 'Over two hundred' is right. The sources measure the borehole, and 'the rock' is fair for bottom-hole formation temperature. The voice does not say the unit, but °C is on screen at the same moment ('212 °C' in both looks). If a viewer assumed Fahrenheit, they would underestimate the heat, not overstate it.

claims.claim: Drilling stopped in nineteen ninety-two, when its funding was cut.
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Zhu & Huang 2026, Commun. Earth Environ. 7: 124, doi:10.1038/s43247-026-03246-z, full text at https://www.nature.com/articles/s43247-026-03246-z (published 3 Feb 2026)
claims.note: Lobanov (EN): "However, a drastic reduction in funding made it impossible to continue the work. Drilling was stopped in 1992." (RU: "резкое сокращение финансирования не позволило продолжить работы. Бурение прекратили в 1992 г."). Also: "In 1992, a unique operation was carried out to install a casing ... to continue drilling the well to a depth of 13 km. However, despite this, further drilling was abandoned." Zhu & Huang give a different cause: "Drilling was abandoned in 1992 when unexpectedly high bottom-hole temperatures of 212 °C induced plastic rock flow that repeatedly sealed the hole." That sentence has no citation (ref. 29 belongs to the sentence before it). Lobanov never mentions plastic flow. The year 1992 is in both sources, and the funding cut is stated by the RAS insiders and contradicted by neither. The disagreement is recorded in SOURCES entry 7, as A3 requires. Pedant risk: commenters may say 'it stopped because of the heat'. The heat is in line 6.

claims.claim: Twelve kilometres down. The centre of the Earth is over six thousand more.
claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html; Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed
claims.note: NSSDC: "Volumetric mean radius (km) 6371.000"; 6,371 - 12.262 = 6,358.7 km. With the fact sheet's equatorial and polar radii (6378.137 and 6356.752 km), the geocentric radius at Kola's 69°25'N (Lobanov) is ~6,359 km, which leaves ~6,347 km. 'Over six thousand' holds either way.

claims.claim: "THE HOLE: 12 KM" / "0.2% of the way. Too thin to draw."
claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html; Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; src/shorts/deepest-hole/index.tsx
claims.note: 12.262/6371 = 0.192% -> 0.2%. At r = 310 px the hole would be 0.6 px deep, so 'too thin to draw' is true. The hole is marked by a ring and is not drawn.

claims.claim: "21 CM BIT" / "the last stretch: under a plate's width", with a loupe where a plate drops over and covers the hole
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; Clarke et al., USGS Open-File Report 86-517 (1986), https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext, 255 pp.); Met Museum collection API, https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/201074

The loupe is an illustration with no scale claim, and the claim it shows (the plate covers the hole) is true.

claims.claim: Depth counter riding the drill head, sub "deepest point so far": 7,263 m at mid-1975, held to early 1976, 9,584 m at mid-1979, 12,066 m at 1984, held to 1989, then 12,262 M at 1989–90; straight lines between
claims.source_checked: Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed
claims.note: Lobanov: "The first stage of drilling was completed in May 1975, when the well reached a depth of 7263 m"; "Then there was a break for almost a year to replace the drilling rig"; "In 1976 ... the second stage of drilling began"; "In June 1979, the well broke the record of 9583 meters held by the US well, reaching a depth of 9584 meters"; "On December 27, 1983, the well depth reached 12000 m"; "In 1983, the well reached a depth of 12066 m"; 1984 string break, "drilling was resumed from a depth of 7000 m"; "it took 6 years to reach 12 km depth again". The linear path passes 12,000 m at ~1983.97, which matches 27 Dec 1983. The 1984-89 hold is the deepest point reached, labelled as such, so it does not imply the bit sat at 12 km. Lobanov contradicts himself on the first stage ('It took 4 years to drill to 7263 m' vs. completed May 1975). The animation follows the dated statement.

claims.claim: "about a third of the crust" (depth tag sub, after 'crust')

claims.claim: "CRUST" / "≈40 km thick here", crust drawn 40 km thick on the same ruler as the hole; "MANTLE" below; 10/20/30 km ruler labels
claims.source_checked: Clarke et al., USGS Open-File Report 86-517 (1986), https://pubs.usgs.gov/of/1986/0517/report.pdf (pdftotext, 255 pp.); src/shorts/deepest-hole/index.tsx (CRUST_KM = 40, same km-per-unit as the shaft)
claims.note: USGS: "Crustal thickness in the vicinity of the corehole was shown to be about 40 km." The 2 km strata lines are a ruler, not mapped geology. Nothing labels them otherwise. The shaft and drill head are drawn wider than to scale so they can be seen, and the loupe and '21 CM BIT' give the true width.

claims.claim: Earth in section: core drawn to 3,485 km and labelled CORE, mantle above, no inner core, crust only as a ~2 px outline; "MANTLE"
claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html; src/scenes/earth.tsx
claims.note: NSSDC: "Core radius (km) 3485", "Volumetric mean radius (km) 6371.000". The core disc is the whole core, inner core included, so leaving the inner-core boundary out is a simplification, not an error. 40 km at r = 310 px is 1.95 px, which matches the 2 px outline. The section is to scale.

claims.claim: "6,371 KM" / "surface to centre"
claims.source_checked: NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet, https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
claims.note: NSSDC volumetric mean radius 6371.000 km. This is the standard mean figure (equatorial 6378.137, polar 6356.752; ~6,359 km at Kola's latitude). It fits a generic surface-to-centre line on a whole-Earth diagram. Optional tightening: sub 'mean, surface to centre'.

claims.claim: 1987 Soviet stamp labelled "THE KOLA BOREHOLE, USSR"; "DEEPEST HOLE"; crop labelled "THE DRILL TOWER"; the stamp's well drawing pasted into the 'goes down' section
claims.source_checked: public/cutout/hole/stamp.jpg viewed; public/SOURCES.json entry (CPA 5892, 25 Nov 1987)
claims.note: The stamp itself reads "кольская сверхглубокая скважина", "ПОЧТА СССР", "1987", "10к". It shows the enclosed derrick tower (the 'DRILL TOWER' crop) and a section of the well with its drill string (the crop box [318,62,100,700]). The labels match what is pictured.

Lobanov: SG-3 is "in the northwestern part of the Kola Peninsula" (69°25'N, 30°44'E). The circle is generous and includes the White Sea coast, but no exact site is claimed.

claims.claim: "THE BIT": a 21 cm black disc drawn to scale against a 25.6 cm Met dinner plate ("DINNER PLATE"), "21 CM BIT"
claims.source_checked: Met Museum collection API, https://collectionapi.metmuseum.org/public/collection/v1/objects/201074; Lobanov, Chicherov & Sharov 2021, doi:10.37482/issn2221-2698.2021.44.267 (doi.org 302 -> arcticandnorth.ru); journal PDFs read: Russian https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/df4/267_284.pdf (pp. 267-284) and English https://arcticandnorth.ru/upload/iblock/61f/44_224_239.pdf; Fig. 5 (p. 276) rendered and viewed; src/shorts/deepest-hole-cutout/index.tsx (BORE_CM/PLATE_CM scaling)

The disc radius is PLATE_R*k with k = (700/804)*(21/25.6), so the ratio is 0.82; the true 21.4/25.6 is 0.84, within 2%. '21 CM' rounds 214 mm. The black disc reads as the bore and is labelled 'THE BIT', which is consistent.
